text:
melissa: Hey @support — AcmeHealth on a Private VPC deployment. Installer fails when pulling model shards and telemetry posts fail. Agent shows TLS errors and some 403s. Can someone help triage?

rajiv: Can you paste the exact error lines from the agent logs? a short copy/paste is fine.

melissa: Agent log snippets: `ERROR: fetch https://registry.redwood.ai/v1/shards/abc - tls: oversized record received` and `POST https://auth.redwood.ai/oauth/token -> 403 Forbidden {\"error\":\"token_not_found\"}`

onprem-eng: Two usual suspects: (1) TLS MITM / corporate TLS inspect (oversized record often) (2) egress SNI/dns rewrite causing requests to land on proxy that returns 302/403. Also possible an HTTP proxy speaking plaintext on 443.

sre-bot: Note: model shards are pulled from `cdn-models.redwood.ai` (may redirect to `s3.amazonaws.com`). Telemetry posts go to `ingest.telemetry.redwood.ai` on 443. OCSP/CRL lookups will be performed to CA endpoints.

melissa: Customer confirmed they have a TLS-inspecting corporate proxy and split-horizon DNS. They cannot globally disable MITM. They asked for a minimal outbound FQDN allowlist and repro steps we can give infra.

rajiv: Minimal allowlist we recommend (TCP 443, preserve SNI/no rewrite). Also allow OCSP/CRL lookups and outbound DNS to their resolver (udp/tcp 53).
```
- auth.redwood.ai (443)         -- OAuth token endpoints
- registry.redwood.ai (443)     -- model registry API
- cdn-models.redwood.ai (443)   -- shard CDN (may redirect to s3)
- s3.amazonaws.com (443)        -- S3 backend for shard storage
- ingest.telemetry.redwood.ai (443) -- telemetry/metrics/traces
- console-metrics.redwood.ai (443) -- metrics/console callbacks
- docker.pkg.redwood.ai (443)  -- installer images
- pypi.org / files.pythonhosted.org (443) -- pip deps
- repo.maven.org (443)         -- java deps if used
- ocsp.globalsign.com (80/443), ocsp.digicert.com (80/443) -- OCSP
```

rajiv: Repro steps to give infra / customer (run from bastion/installer host):
```
# check registry reachability
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://registry.redwood.ai/v1/health
# inspect cert chain (with SNI)
openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername registry.redwood.ai -showcerts
# bypass DNS if split-horizon is wrong (use public IP)
curl -v --resolve registry.redwood.ai:443:52.216.12.34 https://registry.redwood.ai/v1/health
# capture traffic for deep triage (pcap)
sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -w /tmp/egress_registry.pcap 'host registry.redwood.ai and port 443'
```

onprem-eng: If `openssl s_client` shows the corporate intercept cert (subject like "Corp TLS Intercept"), that's MITM. The `oversized record` TLS error often means the proxy is sending HTTP on 443 or doing non-TLS handling. If curl returns 302 to an internal proxy host, that's a sign of interception/redirect.

security: If they cannot remove MITM, two options: (A) get infra to allow direct, non-intercepted egress to the FQDNs above (by SNI/fqdn rules) OR (B) have the customer add their corp MITM CA to the onprem agent truststore (requires formal approval and change control). We logged incident INC-2027-0441 for tracking.

melissa: Customer ran the openssl test: got a cert with Subject CN="Corp TLS Intercept" and curl shows 302 -> `internal-proxy.local`. They're going to request the FQDN allowlist from infra.

onprem-eng: If infra only allows by IP, warn them CDN/AWS IP ranges change. Provide example AWS ranges as fallback (best-effort): `52.216.0.0/14`, `3.5.140.0/22` — but advise to prefer FQDN/SNI rules.

rajiv: Also include these auxiliary telemetry/ops hosts if customer enabled them: `collector-01.telemetry.redwood.ai`, `events.redwood.ai`, `auth-stats.redwood.ai`, and `sentry.io` domains (443). Keep only 443 open.

customer-ops: If they need certificate pinning we can provide the current leaf SHA256 fingerprint on request (we rotate certs in CA windows; will fetch live if they need it).

melissa: I'll send the FQDN list, the curl/openssl reproduction steps, and tcpdump guidance to the customer. Will update ticket with infra response. :thumbsup:
